questions.q: What is the first step in the real Update Set workflow?
options: Mark it Complete
Review the list of captured changes
Set the new Update Set as Current in the picker
Export it as XML
questions.explain: Setting Current has to happen first -- every change made afterward is captured into whichever Update Set is active at that moment.

questions.q: An admin edits a UI Policy, then creates and switches to a new Update Set, then edits an ACL. Where does the UI Policy edit end up?
options: In the new Update Set, alongside the ACL edit
In whatever Update Set was current before the switch -- typically Default
It is discarded and not captured anywhere
It is captured in both Update Sets simultaneously
questions.explain: Changes made before switching Current land in the previously active Update Set, usually Default -- the classic beginner mistake.

questions.q: Why is the Default Update Set described as a trap rather than a feature to use on purpose?
options: It cannot capture any changes at all
It only exists in Development instances
It accumulates unrelated changes over time and is rarely promoted to another instance as-is
It automatically deletes itself after 24 hours
questions.explain: Default is a catch-all fallback, not a container for one piece of scoped work -- finding your work there signals you skipped setting Current first.

questions.q: What should you do right before marking an Update Set Complete?
options: Delete any Script Includes it references
Review its list of captured changes to confirm it holds exactly what you intended
Rename the Default Update Set
Switch the instance to maintenance mode
questions.explain: Reviewing catches both missing intended changes and unrelated changes that snuck in while this Update Set happened to be current.

questions.q: What does marking an Update Set Complete signal, per this lesson?
options: That it has already been committed to Production
That it is finished and ready to export/promote, and in normal practice shouldn't be edited further
That all of its changes have been automatically tested
That it has been permanently deleted from the instance
questions.explain: Complete is a one-way status in normal use -- further related work starts a new Update Set rather than reopening this one.
